```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Load cfbstats from the checkout when the package is not installed, so the
# site build does not require a package install (decision 0030).
if (requireNamespace("cfbstats", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # vignettes render in a fresh quarto R session: attach the installed package
  # (CI installs it via local::.) or source the checkout fallback below.
  library(cfbstats)
} else {
  dir <- getwd()
  while (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "_targets")) && dirname(dir) != dir) {
    dir <- dirname(dir)
  }
  for (src in sort(list.files(file.path(dir, "R"), pattern = "[.]R$", full.names = TRUE))) {
    source(src, local = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
  }
}
library(dplyr)
library(reactable)
library(targets)
root <- cfbstats_root()
if (nzchar(root)) {
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
}
```

This project is built to be **faithful to the raw data and transparent about
every transformation**. Two things support that: a **data dictionary** for each
source, and a **per-step audit log** generated by the pipeline (decision 0005).

The tables in the DuckDB bundle relate like this (the ERD is hand-authored in
[`inst/data-model.md`](https://github.com/ngiangre/cfbstats/blob/main/inst/data-model.md),
derived from the join-namespace decisions — e.g. 0013, 0014 — rather than
generated from the schema; solid lines are trustworthy key joins, the dotted
`recruiting` line is name-guarded, not a plain id join):

```{mermaid}
erDiagram
    player_stats }o--|| roster : "playerId, season"
    player_stats ||--o{ player_season_stats : "pivoted wide (playerId, season, team)"
    player_stats ||--o| picks : "playerId"
    player_stats }o--|| coaches : "team=school, season"
    player_stats }o--|| conference_tiers : "conference, season"
    player_stats }o--|| teams : "team (display)"
    recruiting |o..o| player_stats : "playerId (name-guarded)"
    games ||--o{ game_team_stats : "gameId == id"
    games ||--o{ game_player_stats : "gameId == id"
    game_player_stats }o--|| player_stats : "playerId (shared athlete id)"
    picks ||--o| nfl_pick_link : "same slot join, name-guarded"
    nfl_pick_link ||--o| nfl_draft_picks : "draft slot"
    nfl_draft_picks ||--o{ nfl_rosters : "gsis_id, season"
    nfl_draft_picks ||--o{ nfl_player_stats : "gsis_id, season"
    ps_change }o--|| roster_flags : "playerId, season (flags/weights attach here)"
    roster |o--o{ career_summary : "playerId (collapsed)"
```

## Sources

We build on the [College Football Data](https://collegefootballdata.com) API,
plus [nflverse](https://nflverse.nflreadr.com/) for post-draft NFL outcomes
(rosters, statistics, and career summaries) linked to draft picks by draft slot
(decision 0014). Each dataset has a dictionary (shipped in the package under
`inst/dict/`) describing its grain, key, and columns.

```{r}
#| label: dictionaries
dict_dir <- file.path(root, "inst", "dict")
dict_files <- list.files(dict_dir, pattern = "\\.yml$", full.names = TRUE)
purrr::map_dfr(dict_files, function(f) {
  d <- yaml::read_yaml(f)
  tibble::tibble(
    dataset = d$dataset,
    source = d$source,
    grain = d$grain,
    key = d$key,
    n_columns = length(d$columns)
  )
}) |>
  reactable(searchable = TRUE, striped = TRUE, defaultPageSize = 10)
```

### Column-level detail

```{r}
#| label: dictionary-columns
purrr::map_dfr(dict_files, function(f) {
  d <- yaml::read_yaml(f)
  purrr::map_dfr(d$columns, function(col) {
    tibble::tibble(
      dataset = d$dataset,
      column = col$name,
      type = col$type,
      provenance = col$provenance %||% NA_character_,
      description = col$description
    )
  })
}) |>
  reactable(
    searchable = TRUE,
    filterable = TRUE,
    striped = TRUE,
    groupBy = "dataset",
    defaultPageSize = 15
  )
```

## Querying the DuckDB bundle

Every cleaned and derived table ships in one SQL-queryable file,
`data/cfbstats.duckdb` (published on the `data-latest` GitHub release):

```r
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "data/cfbstats.duckdb", read_only = TRUE)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM _schema_manifest")  # grain + key per table
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM _meta")             # refresh time + last COMPLETE season/draft
```

Besides the documented tables, the bundle carries generated metadata: a
`_schema_manifest` (grain/key read from the dictionaries at build time —
`documented = FALSE` would flag a schema-drift bug), a `_meta` row with
`last_complete_cfb_season` / `last_complete_nfl_draft` (later seasons may be
partial; out-of-time logic should stop at these), a slimmed `audit_log`
(lineage, queryable in SQL), and a `player_season_inputs` VIEW =
`ps_change` minus the draft-outcome columns — the leakage-safe model input
surface. Join-namespace rules and worked SQL examples are in
[`inst/data-model.md`](https://github.com/ngiangre/cfbstats/blob/main/inst/data-model.md);
the wide `player_season_stats` table (one column per stat) means most
statistical questions need no pivoting at all.

## Provenance / audit log

Every tracked pipeline step records a uniform row: input/output row and column
counts, key coverage, join coverage (`pct_keys_matched` / `keys_dropped`),
total and per-column NA cells, a schema hash, and the governing data
contract's pass/fail (decision 0005). This is where **silent join loss and
schema drift become visible**.

::: {.callout-note}
## Column meanings

- `step`, `stage` — the transform and its pipeline stage (ingest → clean → link → features → model → report).
- `n_rows_in` / `n_rows_out` — rows entering and leaving the step (`NA` for the first step of a branch, which has no tracked input).
- `rows_delta` — output rows minus input rows; negative means rows collapsed or filtered, positive means the join fanned out.
- `keys_dropped` — distinct key combinations from the input that no longer appear in the output (`NA` when the step has no tracked input). `0` under a pure fan-out or column addition; positive means rows were filtered away, distinguishing filtering from fan-out.
- `pct_keys_matched` — share of the input's distinct key combinations that survive into the output (join/filter coverage).
- `n_cols_out` — columns in the step's output.
- `n_keys_out` — number of distinct values across the step's declared key columns (key coverage).
- `n_na_cells` — total missing cells in the output; the "top NA columns" column attributes them, since each added column raises this ceiling mechanically.
- `n_cols_with_na` — how many output columns carry at least one missing value.
- `contract_passed` — whether the step's data contract (pointblank validation) passed; `NA` means no contract governs the step.
- `schema_hash` — 12-character digest of the output's column names and types; changes signal schema drift (see the history below).
:::

```{r}
#| label: audit-log
tip <- function(label, title) {
  htmltools::tags$span(label, title = title, style = "cursor: help;")
}
tar_read(audit_log) |>
  select(step, stage, n_rows_in, n_rows_out, rows_delta, keys_dropped,
         pct_keys_matched, n_cols_out, n_keys_out, n_na_cells,
         n_cols_with_na, na_by_col, contract_passed, schema_hash) |>
  reactable(
    striped = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 12,
    columns = list(
      step = colDef(header = tip("step", "Transform name, e.g. link_coaches")),
      stage = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "stage",
          "Pipeline stage: ingest, clean, link, features, model, or report"
        )
      ),
      n_rows_in = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "n_rows_in",
          "Rows entering the step; NA when the step has no tracked input"
        )
      ),
      n_rows_out = colDef(header = tip("n_rows_out", "Rows leaving the step")),
      rows_delta = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "rows_delta",
          "Output rows minus input rows; negative = rows collapsed or filtered, positive = join fanned out"
        ),
        style = function(value) {
          if (is.na(value)) {
            return(NULL)
          }
          if (value < 0) {
            list(color = "#b00020")
          } else if (value > 0) {
            list(color = "#0059b3")
          } else {
            NULL
          }
        }
      ),
      keys_dropped = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "keys dropped",
          "Distinct key combinations from the input absent from the output; 0 = pure fan-out/addition"
        ),
        style = function(value) {
          if (isTRUE(value > 0)) list(color = "#b00020") else NULL
        }
      ),
      pct_keys_matched = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "keys matched",
          "Share of the input's distinct key combinations surviving into the output"
        ),
        format = colFormat(percent = TRUE, digits = 1)
      ),
      n_cols_out = colDef(header = tip("n_cols_out", "Columns in the output")),
      n_keys_out = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "n_keys_out",
          "Distinct values across the step's key columns (key coverage)"
        )
      ),
      n_na_cells = colDef(
        header = tip("n_na_cells", "Total missing cells in the output")
      ),
      n_cols_with_na = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "cols w/ NA",
          "Output columns carrying at least one missing value"
        )
      ),
      na_by_col = colDef(
        name = "top NA columns",
        header = tip(
          "top NA columns",
          "Columns with the most missing values, with their NA rate"
        ),
        sortable = FALSE,
        cell = function(value) {
          if (is.null(value) || nrow(value) == 0) {
            return("")
          }
          paste0(
            head(value$col, 3), " (", round(head(value$na_rate, 3) * 100), "%)",
            collapse = ", "
          )
        }
      ),
      contract_passed = colDef(
        name = "contract",
        header = tip(
          "contract",
          "Did the step's data contract (pointblank validation) pass?"
        )
      ),
      schema_hash = colDef(
        header = tip(
          "schema_hash",
          "Digest of output column names and types; a change signals schema drift"
        )
      )
    )
  )
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Reading the log

- `build_player_season` shows the large negative `rows_delta` where the **long** stats collapse to one identity row per player-season, but `keys_dropped = 0`: every input key survives; the collapse happens within keys.
- `link_coaches` shows a positive `rows_delta` with `keys_dropped = 0`: some schools carry more than one head coach in a season (midseason changes), which fans the join out — row change with no lost keys.
- `filter_reused_ids` drops 462 key combos (coverage ~99.7%): CFBD recycles a few hundred athlete ids across different people over long spans (decision 0022), and these are removed from the model population rather than silently misjoined.
- `career_summary` drops 131 player keys for the same reason — impossible career spans from id reuse.
:::

## Schema history

Each refresh appends one row per step (hash, timestamp, git SHA) to a history
file published on the `data-latest` release, so a change in `schema_hash`
between refreshes — schema drift — is detectable rather than only visible as
an unfamiliar hash in the current log.

```{r}
#| label: schema-history
history <- tar_read(schema_history)
if (is.null(history)) {
  cat("No history yet (track mode with no history file); drift is compared across refreshes.\n")
} else {
  drifted <- history |>
    group_by(step) |>
    filter(n_distinct(schema_hash) > 1) |>
    ungroup()
  if (nrow(drifted) == 0) {
    cat("No schema drift detected across recorded refreshes.\n")
  }
  history |>
    select(step, n_cols_out, schema_hash, timestamp, git_sha) |>
    reactable(
      searchable = TRUE,
      striped = TRUE,
      defaultPageSize = 12,
      columns = list(
        step = colDef(header = tip("step", "Transform name")),
        n_cols_out = colDef(header = tip("n_cols_out", "Columns in the output at that run")),
        schema_hash = colDef(
          header = tip("schema_hash", "Digest of column names and types"),
          style = function(value) {
            if (value %in% drifted$schema_hash) list(background = "#fff3cd") else NULL
          }
        ),
        timestamp = colDef(header = tip("timestamp", "When the refresh ran")),
        git_sha = colDef(header = tip("git_sha", "Code commit that produced the run"))
      )
    )
}
```
